newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae in $25 mln W.Va. bond agreement.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae in $25 mln W.Va. bond agreement.

text.p: Federal National Mortgage Association said Monday it signed a $25 million bond purchase agreement with West Virginia Housing Development Fund.
The deal will provide access for 450 West Virginia families to below-market mortgage rates, Fannie Mae said.

"Homeownership nurtures community pride and gives families a place they can call home," said Sen Jay Rockefeller, a West Virginia Democrat and a proponent of using mortgage revenue bonds for affordable housing programs.
"This is a great example of the type of public-private partnerships that expand the availability of affordable housing for hard working families in our state."
Under the deal, Fannie Mae agreed to buy $25 million of tax-exempt, single-family bonds issued by the West Virginia fund.
The bond proceeds are available through local mortgage lenders statewide to provide financing for 30-year, fixed-rate, FHA and VA mortgages with a below- market interest rate of 6.99 percent.
